    "content": "Title: VECTR Lab - Home\nURL: https://vectr-ucla.github.io/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nVECTR Lab - Home\n\n## Verifiable & Control-Theoretic Robotics Laboratory\n\nUniversity of California, Los Angeles\n\n \n\n High-performance and field-hardened autonomy for mobile robotic systems. \n\nWe are a research group in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at UCLA that specializes in designing autonomy algorithms with formal performance guarantees for mobile robotic systems. We utilize dynamical systems and control theory, optimization, and machine learning to design and verify algorithms that maintain consistent performance across diverse operating domains. Our work is improving the reliability and trustworthiness of autonomous systems that someday will be utilized in space, planetary exploration, emergency response, firefighting, and urban air transport. In addition to rigorous theoretical analysis, our work undergoes extensive field testing on our custom aerial robotic platforms.\n\nSpecific research areas of interests are:\n\n- Localization and Mapping\n- Trajectory Planning and Optimization\n- Nonlinear and Optimal Control\n- Robot Perception\n- Multi-Agent Systems\n- Field Robotics\n\nIf you are interested in joining the lab send an email to Prof. Lopez at btlopez at ucla dot edu with your CV and research interests.\n\n---\n\nTitle: vectr-ucla/vectr-ucla.github.io\nURL: https://github.com/vectr-ucla/vectr-ucla.github.io\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# vectr-ucla/vectr-ucla.github.io\n\n- Stars: 0\n- Forks: 0\n- Watchers: 0\n- Open issues: 0\n- Default branch: master\n- Created: 2022-03-07T03:05:40Z\n\n...\n\n# VECTR Lab Website\n\nThis website is a work in progress. You, as a member of any developer ambassador program, are expected to produce technical content in the form of:\n\n* text (blog posts)\n* audio (podcasts)\n* video (YouTube videos)\n* public speaking (talks at meetups or conferences)\n* Open source contribution to relevant repositories, and\n* helping the community by commenting or answering questions on platforms like StackOverflow\n\n### Benefits of joining a developer ambassador program\n\nThose contributions are unpaid, but you might get other benefits from doing so. The benefits might include\n\n* recognition and personal branding\n* access to features of products and services before the general public\n* invitation and access to the company's special or developer events\n* cover travel and/or accommodation to events where you speak about the company's products\n* special or free access to the company's products or services\n* credits to use the company's products or services\n\n...\n\n* Agentic AI Ambassdor - If you’re passionate about AI and machine learning and love learning, building, sharing knowledge, and helping others grow in the field, join the AAIF Ambassadors program. This is an elite cohort of practitioners helping the world understand, use, and contribute to AAIF-hosted projects.\n* Appwrite Heroes - If you love building, writing, speaking, and helping other developers build with Appwrite, help us support you by joining the Appwrite Heroes program and becoming a leader in our developer community.\n* Auth0 Ambassador - Join us in our mission to advocate for the developer by sharing knowledge on identity and security related topics through meetups, conferences, written content, webinars and other events as an Auth0 Ambassador.\n* AWS Community Builder - The AWS Community Builders program offers technical resources, education, and networking opportunities to AWS technical enthusiasts and emerging thought leaders who are passionate about sharing knowledge and connecting with the technical community.\n* AWS Heroes - The AWS Heroes program recognizes a vibrant, worldwide group of AWS experts whose enthusiasm for knowledge-sharing has a real impact within the community. Heroes go above and beyond to share knowledge in a variety of ways including online via social media, blog posts, open source projects, videos, and forums; or in person at conferences, workshops, and user group events.\n* AWS Student Builder Campus Leader - AWS Student Builder Campus Leaders are paid, part-time student ambassadors who bring AWS Builder Center to life on their campuses by driving awareness of cloud tools and resources, hosting events, creating content, and inspiring peers to start building. * For students only. Unlike most programs on this list it is a paid role, currently available only in the United States, India, and Brazil.\n* AWS Student Builder Group Leader - AWS Student Builder Group Leaders (formerly known as AWS Cloud Club Captains) are student leaders who form and launch AWS Student Builder Groups (formerly AWS Cloud Clubs) with AWS help and support. Group Leaders take on the responsibility to grow their group membership, host events, and support local initiatives. * For students only.\n* BrowserStack Champions - A global community of passionate QA experts, dedicated to advancing software quality, continuous learning, and making an impact in testing and development.\n* Claude Campus Program - Lead student-driven AI initiatives with Anthropic support. Apply to lead a Claude Builder Club or become a Campus Ambassador to advance AI education. If you’re passionate about building student communities, the Claude Builder Club program is for you. Has two programs: the Claude Builder Club program and the Claude Campus Ambassador. * For students only.\n* Claude Community Ambassadors - Build and lead the Claude community in your city. Host local events, bring builders together, and partner with Anthropic to shape the future of Claude. The Claude Community Ambassadors program gives you everything you need to create a thriving community of builders in your city.\n* Cloud Native Ambassadors - CNCF - Cloud Native Ambassadors (CNAs) are credible advocates for the cloud native ecosystem, driven by their passion for CNCF technologies and projects, as well as furthering the mission of open source.\n* Cloudinary Ambassadors - An Ambassador has achieved high-level mastery of digital media technologies, is passionate about sharing their knowledge, and advocates for a better visual web.\n* Codex Ambassadors - Codex Ambassadors are community organizers, open-source maintainers, student leaders, and power users who actively spread what works, make Codex easier to adopt in practice, and help shape where it goes next. Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent for software development. \n* Commudle Experts - A Commudle expert can be a student or a professional, a freelancer, full time techie, DevRel or a Dev Advocate. Your qualification or location doesn't matter, your work does!\n* Cursor Ambassador Program - Become a Cursor Ambassador. Join our community of developers who help shape the future of AI-powered coding. Cursor Ambassadors empower the community that makes our ecosystem vibrant and collaborative.\n* Cypress Ambassadors - Ambassadors go the extra mile—sharing their knowledge through blog posts, articles, webcasts, conferences, meetups, and other events.\n* DeepLearning.ai event Ambassador - Our Event Ambassadors are enthusiastic about helping more cities become Al hubs and inspiring their local community to break into Al. Help build the global Al community by representing your area.\n* Devin.ai Ambassador - Lead the Devin community in your city. Host events, create content, and shape what comes next.\n* DigitalOcean's Navigators - Supports and rewards people who create content, code, and/or community engagements related to DigitalOcean’s products and services.\n* Docker Captains - Docker Captains are technical experts and passionate community builders who drive Docker’s ecosystem forward. As active contributors and advocates, they share Docker knowledge and help shape Docker products.\n* ElevenLabs Ambassador Program - Help the world discover what is possible with ElevenLabs by joining the ElevenLabs Ambassador Program. Create content, host events, and champion ElevenLabs in your community. See Academic email requirements below.\n- Own a GitHub personal account.\n- Are at least 13 years old.\n\n## What documents can I use to prove I'm a student?\n\n- A picture of your school ID with current enrollment date\n- Your class schedule\n- Your transcript\n- An affiliation or enrollment verification letter\n\n## Academic email requirements\n\nGitHub's verification process is individually tailored. When the system detects that recent applicants from your school successfully verified using their academic email, future applicants from the same school must also use an academic email.\n\n### Your school requires an academic email address\n\nIf the application asks for an academic email, you must add and verify one on your GitHub account before applying. See Adding an email address to your GitHub account.\n\n### Your school does not provide an academic email address\n\nIf your institution does not issue academic emails, provide official documentation, such as a school webpage or a letter on school letterhead, explaining the policy. Then reapply for GitHub Education.\n\n### Your school's email domain is not recognized\n\nIf your school email domain is not recognized in the application, contact GitHub Education Support with your school's full name, website URL, and the email domain you are attempting to use.\n\n## Applying to GitHub Education\n\n1. Navigate to your Education benefits settings.\n2. Under \"GitHub Education\", click Start an application.\n3. Complete the form, then click Submit application.\n\nOnce your application is approved, navigate to your GitHub Education portal to use your GitHub Education benefits, such as free access to professional developer tools.\n\n---\n\nTitle: About GitHub Education for students\nURL: https://docs.github.com/en/education/about-github-education/github-education-for-students/about-github-education-for-students\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# About GitHub Education for students\n\nGitHub Education offers students real-world experience with free access to various developer tools from GitHub's partners.\n\nAs a student or faculty member at an accredited educational institution, you can apply for GitHub Education. GitHub Education is a portal that allows the GitHub Education Community to access their education benefits—all in one place! The GitHub Education portal includes access to the GitHub Education Community, industry tools used by professional developers, events, GitHub Classroom, GitHub Community Exchange, GitHub Student Developer Pack, and other exclusive features to help students and teachers shape the next generation of software development.\n\nUsing GitHub for your school projects is a practical way to collaborate with others and build a portfolio that showcases real-world experience.\n\nEveryone with a GitHub account can collaborate in unlimited public and private repositories with GitHub Free. As a student, you can also apply for GitHub Education student benefits. Your GitHub Education student benefits and resources are all included in GitHub Education, a portal that allows you to access your education benefits, all in one place. For more information, see Apply to GitHub Education as a student and GitHub Education.\n\nBefore applying for GitHub Education, check if your learning community is already partnered with us as a GitHub Campus Program school. For more information on campus experts, see About GitHub Campus Experts.\n- Gain in-depth understanding of a feature, tool, or topic with curated experiences designed to support your learning journey.\n- Explore and claim offers for free industry tools from the Student Developer Pack.\n- See upcoming in-person and virtual events for students, curated by GitHub Education and student leaders.\n- View assignments from GitHub Classroom with upcoming due dates.\n- Stay in the know on what the community is interested in by rewatching recent Campus TV episodes. Campus TV is created by GitHub and student community leaders and can be watched live or on demand.\n- Discover student-created repositories from GitHub Community Exchange. For more information, see About GitHub Community Exchange.\n\nGitHub Education students also receive the following GitHub benefits.\n\n- GitHub Copilot: Verified students get free access to Copilot and its premium features. See Access GitHub Copilot for free as a student.\n- GitHub Codespaces: Verified students get free use of GitHub Codespaces, up to 180 core hours per month, for their personal accounts. The monthly amount of storage and core hours of usage available to students is equivalent to the amount included with GitHub Pro accounts. For more information, see GitHub Codespaces billing. （华为云学生开发者计划）Huawei Cloud Student A friend joining the server and setting you as their Inviter will earn 100 XP. There will also be activities, tasks, and competitions you can participate in which will earn you XP Bonuses.\n\nWhen certain levels of XP are achieved, you will gain a new Ambassador Rank and unlock new activities, opportunities, and perks.\n\nAdditionally each month the user with the most XP earned will win the title of King/Queen of the Server, giving them top tier perks for 30 days. Discord recently changed their Terms & Conditions meaning that tracking invite links became a banned activity. Instead, those you invite have to manually indicate that you are the one that invited them.\n\nThe process you need to follow is:\n\n1 — Create an invite link to the #check-tier channel\n\n2 — Give this link to your friend 3 — When they join the server, they must run this command rank!m @yourDiscordTag set inviter. Each person can only run the command once, but there is no limit on the number of times you can be set as the inviter.\n\nWhat are the XP Levels and Ambassador Ranks?\n\nWhat do the Ambassador Ranks get me?\n\nMinidebutant\n\n- Access to all public channels\n- Access to Update AMAs on the Minima Stage\n\nMinimalists\n\n- Access to public channels\n- Access to Update AMAs on the Minima Stage\n- Access to Ambassador Lounge\n\nMaximalists\n\n- Access to public channels\n- Access to Update AMAs on the Minima Stage\n- Access to Ambassador Lounge\n- Access to Ambassador Task Channel\n- Participation in Early Access Program\n- Invites to Ambassador Only Events\n- 5% off Minima Merch\n\nMinima Ambassadors\n\n- Access to public channels\n- Access to Update AMAs on the Minima Stage\n- Access to Ambassador Lounge\n- Access to Ambassador Task Channel\n- Participation in Early Access Program\n- Invites to Ambassador Only Events\n- 10% off Minima Merch\n- Access to Ambassador Bounty Channel\n\nMinima Grand Ambassadors\n\n- Access to public channels\n- Access to Update AMAs on the Minima Stage\n- Access to Ambassador Lounge\n- Access to Ambassador Task Channel\n- Participation in Early Access Program\n- Invites to Ambassador Only Events\n- 10% off Minima Merch\n- Access to Ambassador Bounty Channel\n- Social Sessions with Minima Team\n\nWhat is The Ambassador Lounge?\n\nA private space for Minimalists & above to get hyped, share advice, coordinate and share Ambassador success stories. ByteChef stores everything in an embedded H2 file under `~/.bytechef`, next to the generated encryption keys:\n\n```bash\ndocker run --name bytechef -it -p 8080:8080 \\\n    --env BYTECHEF_DATABASE=h2 \\\n    --env BYTECHEF_AI_MEMORY_PROVIDER=in_memory \\\n    -v ~/.bytechef:/root/.bytechef \\\n    docker.bytechef.io/bytechef/bytechef:latest\n```\n\nOn Windows PowerShell:\n\n```powershell\ndocker run --name bytechef -it -p 8080:8080 --env BYTECHEF_DATABASE=h2 -v \"$HOME\\.bytechef:/root/.bytechef\" docker.bytechef.io/bytechef/bytechef:latest\n```\n\nOpen → **Create Account** → sign in.\n\n**First workflow, no credentials needed:** import Learn ByteChef by doing from the template library and run it.\n\n...\n\nThe AI knowledge base and Copilot need PostgreSQL with pgvector, and there is no migration path from H2 to PostgreSQL, so use Docker Compose for anything you intend to keep.\n\n...\n\n### Then build your first agent\n\nAn agent needs a model. Connect any of the 12 LLM providers with an API key, or run Ollama locally and connect it with no key at all. Write the instructions and configure each tool's parameters in the properties panel\n7. Click **Test** and read the agent's tool calls in the execution log\n8. Deploy\n\n...\n\nWant a connector we don't have? You build workflows in a visual editor, from a library of more than 270 connectors and flow controls, and add code steps in JavaScript, Python or Java where a connector is not enough. AI agents are first-class workflow steps: give an agent a model, tools drawn from the same connectors, memory and guardrails, and let it act inside a workflow that you can pause for a human approval and resume. The same engine can be embedded in your own product, so your customers connect their accounts and run integrations without leaving your app.\n\nThese docs are organized by what you want to do. Platform explains how to use ByteChef, from your first workflow to enterprise settings. The Reference documents every component, its actions and triggers, and the expression syntax used to pass data between steps. The Developer Guide covers running ByteChef from source and building your own connectors, and the API reference describes the public REST APIs for automation, embedded integrations and custom components. Agents can read any page as markdown by requesting it with `Accept: text/markdown`, and start from llms.txt.\n\n## Choose how to use ByteChef [#choose-how-to-use-bytechef]\n\n\" title=\"Cloud\" href=\"/platform/use-bytechef/cloud\">\nRun ByteChef on our managed, hosted deployment - no infrastructure to manage.\n\n\" title=\"Self-Hosted\" href=\"/platform/use-bytechef/self-hosted\">\nDeploy and operate ByteChef on your own infrastructure - Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or DigitalOcean.\n\n## Pick your path [#pick-your-path]\n\n\" title=\"Automation\" href=\"/platform/automation/get-started\">\nEasily build and run smart workflows that connect your apps, automate routine tasks, and include AI-driven decisions-no heavy coding needed.\n\n\" title=\"Embedded\" href=\"/platform/embedded/get-started\">\nBring the power of ByteChef directly into your product-embed the workflow builder, run automations behind the scenes, and let your users create workflows inside your app.\n\n## Explore more [#explore-more]\n\n\" title=\"Developer Guide\" href=\"/developer-guide\">\nBuild a component by hand or generate one from an OpenAPI specification, and learn the DSL for actions, triggers, connections, and properties.\n\n\" title=\"Reference\" href=\"/reference\">\nEvery component and flow control, plus the expression syntax and its built-in functions.\n\n## Community support [#community-support]\n\nFor help, you can use one of these channels to ask a question:\n\n- Discord - \n\nHuawei Cloud Student Developers（华为云学生开发者计划，简称HCSD），是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，帮助开发者学习提升，推动高校生态的构建和发展。\n\nHuawei Cloud Student Developers（华为云学生开发者计划，简称HCSD），是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，帮助开发者学习提升，推动高校生态的构建和发展。\n\n### 3年成立时间\n\n从2022年开始，HCSD已成立3年\n\n### 200+位校园大使\n\n截止目前HCSD已吸纳200+多位校园大使\n\n### 点亮50+所城市\n\n含北京、上海、深圳等50+一二线城市\n\n### 170+所高校\n\n覆盖170+所高校，10万名学生开发者\n\n...\n\n### 校园大使权益\n\n校园大使分为初级、中级、领袖级3个等级，权益随等级划分\n\n- \n\n## 校园大使赋能&指导\n\n由华为云技术专家不定期组织校园大使赋能，传授产品技术使用能力，助力校园大使校内组织活动\n\n 全员权益 \n- \n\n## 华为官方大会门票\n\n尊享华为官方大会如HDC、HC开发者年度盛典等官方活动参与资格及门票（不包含机酒等差旅费）\n\n 全员权益 \n- \n\n## 官方证书\n\n申请通过校园大使后，根据保级/晋级规则，颁发对应证书\n\n 全员权益 \n- \n\n## 校园大使见面会\n\n年度组织优秀校园大使参观华为园区（不包差旅）不少于10人组织/次 \n\n 全员权益 \n- \n\n## 品牌打造\n\n优先邀请官方大会/线下沙龙等渠道演讲、布道；官网页面进行展示，宣传个人品牌魅力\n\n 中级/领袖级专享 \n-\n\n...\n\n优先体验、试用华为云产品或服务的各项扶持计划，校园内组织活动可申请活动物料/礼品\n\n...\n\n### 愿景与使命\n\n技术布道\n\n参与线上线下技术活动、大会、大赛，作为主讲人围绕华为技术开放能力分享经验和案例\n\n技术实践\n\n不断了解学习华为云技术新的开放能力，保持对华为云技术开放能力演进的及时跟进\n\n生态共建\n\n① 积极推广华为云开发者生态，在开源社区/开发者社区积极发布宣传华为云技术，帮助学生提升技术能力\n\n② 在校内组建学生技术社团或担任技术社团负责人/核心成员，定期组织技术学习，开展技术交流，活跃技术社区\n\n③ 协助华为云进行学生开发者计划推广，识别和推荐符合条件的校园大使候选人，壮大校园大使队伍\n\n...\n\n### 校园大使-晋级机制\n\n| 评估维度 | 说明 | 初级 | 中级 | 领袖级 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 学校/学院背书﻿ 熟悉掌握一项或多项华为云开放能力（必备）\n\n⑤ 作为高校技术社团的组织者或核心成员，具备带领和指导社团成员围绕华为技术开放能力进行学习、交流和创新实践的经验\n\n⑥ 利用华为技术开放能力在开发者社区/开源社区有一定的成果和技术影响力\n\n⑦ 多次主导组织或参与技术相关活动/大赛，并取得一定成绩\n\n⑧ 具备一定的组织能力，有协助开展校园开发者活动、推广大赛和雇主品牌的经历。\n\n...\n\n## 常见问题\n\nHCSD是一个什么样的组织？\n\nHCSD （华为云学生开发者计划）Huawei Cloud Student Developers是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，通过互动交流、学习内容共享、实践项目建设，影响并帮助高校学生在云服务领域进行学习和创新。\n\n成为校园大使需要具备的条件？\n\n1.必须是在校学生，校园达人，有一定的影响力，计算机协会/技术社团负责人优先；\n\n2.计算机/信息技术相关专业；热爱前沿技术和开发，认可华为云开发者生态，勇于探索，敢于创新；\n\n3.执行力MAX，有想法，有创意，社交技能强，善于团队协作，乐于分享；\n\n4.具备团队管理运营能力，包括活动组织、扩大HCSD规模、提升HCSD成员数等；\n\n如何选拔华为云校园大使？\n\n华为云校园大使可以通过两种方式选拔：第一种是由华为合作院校推荐，第二种是由个人自主申请。两种方式提交上来的候选人都需要经过资格初审、专家复审/面试/综合终评最终选拔出华为云校园大使。\n\n审核结果何时以什么方式公布？\n\n个人自主申请审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，30个工作日内完成审核；华为合作院校推荐的审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，15个工作日内完成审核。\n\n华为云校园大使有效期多长？\n\n华为云校园大使从获得认证的日期开始，一个自然年为一个认证周期，在此期间，享有华为云校园大使荣誉称号及相应权益；到期后，将根据期间的贡献和成就，重新评估华为云校园大使的资格。\n\n---\n\nTitle: For now, we’re working with schools that have an MLH presence on campus. It builds a semantic graph of your codebase — files, symbols, imports, call chains — and pre-loads exactly the right code into every prompt before your AI sees it.\n\n> The launcher scripts in this repo are Apache 2.0. The graph engine (`graperoot` pip package) is proprietary.\n\n...\n\n## Supported AI Tools\n\n| Tool | Command | Status |\n|------|---------|--------|\n| Claude Code | `dgc` | ✅ Full support |\n| OpenAI Codex CLI | `dg` | ✅ Full support |\n| Cursor | `graperoot . --cursor` | ✅ Full support |\n| Gemini CLI | `graperoot . --gemini` | ✅ Full support |\n| OpenCode | `graperoot . --opencode` / `dgo` | ✅ Full support |\n| GitHub Copilot | `graperoot . --copilot` | ✅ Full support |\n| OpenClaw | `graperoot . --openclaw` | ✅ Full support |\n| Kilocode | `graperoot . --kilocode` | ✅ Full support |\n| MiMo Code | `graperoot . --mimocode` | ✅ Full support |\n| Antigravity | `graperoot . --antigravity` | ✅ Full support |\n| Kiro CLI | `graperoot . --kiro` | ✅ Full support |\n| Command Code | `graperoot .\n\n...\n\n## Install\n\n**macOS / Linux:**\n```bash\ncurl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunal12203/Codex-CLI-Compact/main/install.sh | bash\nsource ~/.zshrc   # or ~/.bashrc / ~/.profile\n```\n\n**Windows (PowerShell):**\n```powershell\nirm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunal12203/Codex-CLI-Compact/main/install.ps1 | iex\n```\n\n**Windows (Scoop):**\n```powershell\nscoop bucket add dual-graph https://github.com/kunal12203/scoop-dual-graph\nscoop install dual-graph\n```\n\n> **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+, Node.js 18+, and one of the supported AI tools.     "content": "Title: pykaldi/pykaldi\nURL: https://github.com/pykaldi/pykaldi/\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# pykaldi/pykaldi\n\nA Python wrapper for Kaldi\n\n- Stars: 1039\n- Forks: 247\n- Watchers: 1039\n- Open issues: 67\n- License: Apache License 2.0\n- Homepage: https://pykaldi.github.io\n- Default branch: master\n- Created: 2017-06-19T18:05:19Z\n\n...\n\nPyKaldi is a Python scripting layer for the [Kaldi] speech recognition toolkit.\nIt provides easy-to-use, low-overhead, first-class Python wrappers for the C++\ncode in Kaldi and [OpenFst] libraries. You can use PyKaldi to write Python code\nfor things that would otherwise require writing C++ code such as calling\nlow-level Kaldi functions, manipulating Kaldi and OpenFst objects in code or\nimplementing new Kaldi tools.\n\n...\n\n## Getting Started\n\nLike Kaldi, PyKaldi is primarily intended for speech recognition researchers and\nprofessionals. It is jam packed with goodies that one would need to build Python\nsoftware taking advantage of the vast collection of utilities, algorithms and\ndata structures provided by Kaldi and OpenFst libraries.\n\nIf you are not familiar with FST-based speech recognition or have no interest in\nhaving access to the guts of Kaldi and OpenFst in Python, but only want to run a\npre-trained Kaldi system as part of your Python application, do not fret.\nPyKaldi includes a number of high-level application oriented modules, such as\n[`asr`], [`alignment`] and [`segmentation`], that should be accessible to most\nPython programmers.\n\nIf you are interested in using PyKaldi for research or building advanced ASR\napplications, you are in luck. PyKaldi comes with everything you need to read,\nwrite, inspect, manipulate or visualize Kaldi and OpenFst objects in Python. It\nincludes Python wrappers for most functions and methods that are part of the\npublic APIs of Kaldi and OpenFst C++ libraries. If you want to read/write files\nthat are produced/consumed by Kaldi tools, check out I/O and table utilities in\nthe [`util`] package. If you want to work with Kaldi matrices and vectors, e.g.\nconvert them to [NumPy] ndarrays and vice versa, check out the [`matrix`]\n\n...\n\nIf you want to use Kaldi for feature extraction and transformation,\ncheck out the [`feat`], [`ivector`] and [`transform`] packages. If you want to\nwork with lattices or other FST structures produced/consumed by Kaldi tools,\ncheck out the [`fstext`], [`lat`] and [`kws`] packages. If you want low-level\naccess to Gaussian mixture models, hidden Markov models or phonetic decision\ntrees in Kaldi, check out the [`gmm`], [`sgmm2`], [`hmm`], and [`tree`]\npackages. If you want low-level access to Kaldi neural network models, check out\nthe [`nnet3`], [`cudamatrix`] and [`chain`] packages. If you want to use the\ndecoders and language modeling utilities in Kaldi, check out the [`decoder`],\n[`lm`], [`rnnlm`], [`tfrnnlm`] and [`online2`] packages.\n\n...\n\n## Projects using PyKaldi\n\nShennong - a toolbox for speech features extraction, like MFCC, PLP etc. using PyKaldi.\n\nKaldi model server - a threaded kaldi model server for live decoding. Can directly decode speech from your microphone with a nnet3 compatible model. Example models for English and German are available. Uses the PyKaldi online2 decoder.\n\nMeetingBot - example of a web application for meeting transcription and summarization that makes use of a pykaldi/kaldi-model-server backend to display ASR output in the browser.\n\n...\n\n## Contributing\n\nWe appreciate all contributions! If you find a bug, feel free to open an issue\nor a pull request. If you would like to request or add a new feature please open\nan issue for discussion.\n\n---\n\nTitle: pykaldi/kaldi\nURL: https://github.com/pykaldi/kaldi\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n# pykaldi/kaldi\n\nPyKaldi compatible fork of Kaldi\n\n- Stars: 3\n- Forks: 11\n- Watchers: 3\n- Open issues: 1\n- License: Other\n- Default branch: master\n- Created: 2017-11-21T04:26:56Z\n- Fork: yes\n\n...\n\nBuild Status\n\nKaldi Speech Recognition Toolkit\n================================\n\nTo build the toolkit: see `./INSTALL`. dynamic compute infrastructure for secure, stateful AI agent execution\n\n- Website: https://tensorlake.ai\n- Email: support@tensorlake.ai\n- Followers: 110\n- Public Repos: 35\n- Created: serverless runtime for sandboxes and deploying background agentic applications\n\n- Stars: 1025\n- Forks: 150\n- Watchers: 1025\n- Open issues: 65\n- License: Apache License 2.0\n- Homepage: https://tensorlake.ai\n- Default branch: main\n- Created: 2024-11-15T08:45:14Z\n\n...\n\n## README\n\n \n \n\n \n\n Build agents with sandboxes and serverless orchestration runtime \n \n\nPyPI Version\nPython Support\nLicense\nDocumentation\nSlack\n\n \n\nTensorlake is a compute infrastructure platform for building agentic applications with sandboxes.\n\nThe Sandbox API creates MicroVM sandboxes which you can use to run agents, or use them as an isolated environment for running tools or LLM generated code.\n\nIn addition to stateful VMs, you can also add long running orchestration capabilities to Agents using a serverless function runtime with fan-out capabilities.\n\n...\n\n### Python SDK Installation\n\n```bash\npip install tensorlake\n```\n\n...\n\nThe `tl` CLI is distributed as a standalone binary, not through PyPI or npm.\nInstall it with the install script:\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://tensorlake.ai/install | sh\n```\n\n### Setup\n\nSign up at cloud.tensorlake.ai and get your API key.\n\n```bash\nexport TENSORLAKE_API_KEY=\"your-api-key\"\ntl login\n```\n\n...\n\n## Orchestrate\n\nCreate orchestration APIs on a distributed runtime with automatic scaling, fan-out capabilities and built-in tracking. The orchestration APIs can be invoked using HTTP requests or using the Python SDK.\n\n### Quickstart\n\nDecorate your entrypoint with `@application()` and functions with `@function()`. Each function runs in its own isolated sandbox.\n\n**Example**: City guide using OpenAI Agents with web search and code execution:\n\n```python\nfrom agents import Agent, Runner\nfrom agents.tool import WebSearchTool, function_tool\nfrom tensorlake.applications import application, function, Image\n\n# Define the image with necessary dependencies\nFUNCTION_CONTAINER_IMAGE = Image(base_image=\"python:3.11-slim\", name=\"city_guide_image\").run(\n    \"pip install openai openai-agents\"\n)\n\n@function_tool\n@function(\n    description=\"Gets the weather for a city using an OpenAI Agent with web search\",\n    secrets=[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"],\n    image=FUNCTION_CONTAINER_IMAGE,\n)\ndef get_weather_tool(city: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Uses an OpenAI Agent with WebSearchTool to find current weather.\"\"\"\n    agent = Agent(\n        name=\"Weather Reporter\",\n        instructions=\"Use web search to find current weather in Fahrenheit for the city.\",\n        tools=[WebSearchTool()],  # Agent can search the web\n    )\n    result = Runner.run_sync(agent, f\"City: {city}\")\n    return result.final_output.strip()\n\n@application(tags={\"type\": \"example\", \"use_case\": \"city_guide\"})\n@function(\n    description=\"Creates a guide with temperature conversion using function_tool\",\n    secrets=[\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"],\n    image=FUNCTION_CONTAINER_IMAGE,\n)\ndef city_guide_app(city: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Uses an OpenAI Agent with function_tool to run Python code for conversion.\"\"\"\n\n    @function_tool\n    def convert_to_celsius_tool(python_code: str) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Converts Fahrenheit to Celsius - runs as Python code via Agent.\"\"\"\n        return float(eval(python_code))\n\n    agent = Agent(\n        name=\"Guide Creator\",\n        instructions=\"Using the appropriate tools, get the weather for the purposes of the guide. If the city uses Celsius, call convert_to_celsius_tool to convert the temperature, passing in the code needed to convert the temperature to Celsius. Create a friendly guide that references the temperature of the city in Celsius if the city typically uses Celsius, otherwise reference the temperature in Fahrenheit. Only reference Celsius or Fahrenheit, not both.\",\n        tools=[get_weather_tool, convert_to_celsius_tool],  # Agent can execute this Python function\n    )\n    result = Runner.run_sync(agent, f\"City: {city}\")\n    return result.final_output.strip()\n```\n\n#### Deploy to Tensorlake\n\n1. Set your API keys:\n```bash\nexport TENSORLAKE_API_KEY=\"your-api-key\"\ntl secrets set OPENAI_API_KEY \"your-openai-key\"\n```\n\n2. Deploy:\n```bash\ntl deploy examples/readme_example/city_guide.py\n```\n\n`tl deploy` builds a version-scoped runtime image for every function and stores\nits registered sandbox-template name in the application manifest. The image\ncontains the dependencies declared by `Image`, the language runner, and the native\nfunction-agent core. Application source remains a separate ZIP that is uploaded\nwith the manifest; it is not copied into the runtime image. Reusing an\napplication version with different code or configuration is rejected; an\nidentical redeploy is idempotent.\nImage and application requests normally route through `TENSORLAKE_API_URL` so\ningress can authenticate them and attach trusted project identity. Application\ndeployment, invocation, output, listing, and inspection all use that same\norigin. Trusted split local installations can set `TENSORLAKE_IMAGE_SERVICE_URL`\nand `TENSORLAKE_FUNCTION_SERVICE_URL` independently.\n\n...\n\n#### Call via HTTP\n\n```bash\n# Invoke the application\ncurl https://api.tensorlake.ai/applications/city_guide_app \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TENSORLAKE_API_KEY\" \\\n  --json '\"San Francisco\"'\n# Returns: {\"request_id\": \"beae8736ece31ef9\"}\n\n# Get the result\ncurl https://api.tensorlake.ai/applications/city_guide_app/requests/{request_id}/output \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TENSORLAKE_API_KEY\"\n\n# Stream results with SSE\ncurl https://api.tensorlake.ai/applications/city_guide_app \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TENSORLAKE_API_KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\n  --json '\"San Francisco\"'\n\n```\n\n...\n\n**What is Tensorlake?**\nTensorlake is the sandbox-native cloud for AI agents — a compute platform for securely running untrusted, LLM-generated code in isolated sandboxes and orchestrating agentic applications at scale.\n\n...\n\n**How do I run code interpreter / tool execution for an LLM agent?**\nSpin up a sandbox as an isolated execution environment for an agent's tools or generated code, run commands or processes inside it, read and write files, and terminate it when done — all from the Python or TypeScript SDK, or the CLI.\n\n**What languages and interfaces are supported?**\nTensorlake provides a Python SDK, a TypeScript SDK, and a standalone CLI (`tl`), plus an HTTP API for invoking orchestration applications.\n\n**How do I get started?**\nSign up at cloud.tensorlake.ai, run `pip install tensorlake` for the Python SDK, install the CLI with `curl -fsSL https://tensorlake.ai/install | sh`, set your `TENSORLAKE_API_KEY`, and create your first sandbox. See the documentation for full guides.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Tensorlake - DEV Community\nURL: https://dev.to/tensorlake\nPublished: 2025-05-12T18:41:01.000Z\nAuthor: Shrijal Acharya Follow\nHighlights:\nTensorlake - DEV Community\n\n# Tensorlake \n\nComposable infrastructure for AI agents\n\nIsolated sandboxes, hosted Git, and a versioned filesystem for deploying agent harnesses, running RL rollouts and evals, and building CI that scales.\n\n tensorlake.ai San Francisco, CA Joined on May 12, 2025 contact@tensorlake.ai \n\n### Meet the team \n\n Shrijal Acharya \n\nNov 1\n\n## 7 Best Code Execution APIs for AI Agents in 2026 \n\nEverything you need to know about OpenAI GPT-5.4 ✌️\n\n Shrijal Acharya \n\nMar 21\n\n---\n\nTitle: Issues · tensorlakeai/tensorlake · GitHub\nURL: https://github.com/tensorlakeai/tensorlake/issues\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\n· Filter by author eabatalov opened\n\non Oct 27, 2026\n- ### Add an opt-in Parallel Search MCP path to the city-guide example\n\ntensorlakeai/tensorlake#1034\n\n · Filter by author georgeatparallel opened\n\non Oct 16, 2026\n- ### Genesis Cohort: get paid for the agents you're building (first 50 devs, 0% commission)\n\ntensorlakeai/tensorlake#983\n\n · Filter by author WT-Agent opened\n\non Sep 24, 2026\n- ### OrcaRouter provider support for Tensorlake agent workloads\n\n---\n\nTitle: Careers | Tensorlake\nURL: https://tensorlake-staging-6ae1c4b654acf9edd033.webflow.io/careers\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nCareers | Tensorlake\n\nTHE MISSION:\n\nOur core mission at Tensorlake is to unlock your data wherever it is. 在学校成立HCSD社团或可将HCSD挂靠至计算机协会/技术社团等单位，并邀请一名本校在职老师作为HCSD指导老师（必备）\n\n③ 已签署华为开发者协议并加入华为开发者计划（必备）\n\n④ 熟悉掌握一项或多项华为云开放能力（必备）\n\n⑤ 作为高校技术社团的组织者或核心成员，具备带领和指导社团成员围绕华为技术开放能力进行学习、交流和创新实践的经验\n\n⑥ 利用华为技术开放能力在开发者社区/开源社区有一定的成果和技术影响力\n\n⑦ 多次主导组织或参与技术相关活动/大赛，并取得一定成绩\n\n⑧ 具备一定的组织能力，有协助开展校园开发者活动、推广大赛和雇主品牌的经历。\n\n...\n\n## 常见问题\n\nHCSD是一个什么样的组织？\n\nHCSD （华为云学生开发者计划）Huawei Cloud Student Developers是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，通过互动交流、学习内容共享、实践项目建设，影响并帮助高校学生在云服务领域进行学习和创新。\n\n成为校园大使需要具备的条件？\n\n1.必须是在校学生，校园达人，有一定的影响力，计算机协会/技术社团负责人优先；\n\n2.计算机/信息技术相关专业；热爱前沿技术和开发，认可华为云开发者生态，勇于探索，敢于创新；\n\n3.执行力MAX，有想法，有创意，社交技能强，善于团队协作，乐于分享；\n\n4.具备团队管理运营能力，包括活动组织、扩大HCSD规模、提升HCSD成员数等；\n\n如何选拔华为云校园大使？\n\n华为云校园大使可以通过两种方式选拔：第一种是由华为合作院校推荐，第二种是由个人自主申请。两种方式提交上来的候选人都需要经过资格初审、专家复审/面试/综合终评最终选拔出华为云校园大使。\n\n审核结果何时以什么方式公布？\n\n个人自主申请审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，30个工作日内完成审核；华为合作院校推荐的审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，15个工作日内完成审核。\n\n华为云校园大使有效期多长？\n\n华为云校园大使从获得认证的日期开始，一个自然年为一个认证周期，在此期间，享有华为云校园大使荣誉称号及相应权益；到期后，将根据期间的贡献和成就，重新评估华为云校园大使的资格。\n\n---\n\nTitle: 在学校成立HCSD社团或可将HCSD挂靠至计算机协会/技术社团等单位，并邀请一名本校在职老师作为HCSD指导老师（必备）\n\n③ 已签署华为开发者协议并加入华为开发者计划（必备）\n\n④ 熟悉掌握一项或多项华为云开放能力（必备）\n\n⑤ 作为高校技术社团的组织者或核心成员，具备带领和指导社团成员围绕华为技术开放能力进行学习、交流和创新实践的经验\n\n⑥ 利用华为技术开放能力在开发者社区/开源社区有一定的成果和技术影响力\n\n⑦ 多次主导组织或参与技术相关活动/大赛，并取得一定成绩\n\n⑧ 具备一定的组织能力，有协助开展校园开发者活动、推广大赛和雇主品牌的经历。\n\n...\n\n## 常见问题\n\nHCSD是一个什么样的组织？\n\nHCSD （华为云学生开发者计划）Huawei Cloud Student Developers是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，通过互动交流、学习内容共享、实践项目建设，影响并帮助高校学生在云服务领域进行学习和创新。\n\n成为校园大使需要具备的条件？\n\n1.必须是在校学生，校园达人，有一定的影响力，计算机协会/技术社团负责人优先；\n\n2.计算机/信息技术相关专业；热爱前沿技术和开发，认可华为云开发者生态，勇于探索，敢于创新；\n\n3.执行力MAX，有想法，有创意，社交技能强，善于团队协作，乐于分享；\n\n4.具备团队管理运营能力，包括活动组织、扩大HCSD规模、提升HCSD成员数等；\n\n如何选拔华为云校园大使？\n\n华为云校园大使可以通过两种方式选拔：第一种是由华为合作院校推荐，第二种是由个人自主申请。两种方式提交上来的候选人都需要经过资格初审、专家复审/面试/综合终评最终选拔出华为云校园大使。\n\n审核结果何时以什么方式公布？\n\n个人自主申请审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，30个工作日内完成审核；华为合作院校推荐的审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，15个工作日内完成审核。\n\n华为云校园大使有效期多长？\n\n华为云校园大使从获得认证的日期开始，一个自然年为一个认证周期，在此期间，享有华为云校园大使荣誉称号及相应权益；到期后，将根据期间的贡献和成就，重新评估华为云校园大使的资格。\n\n---\n\nTitle: It has to answer with one self-contained `world.html` that renders the world in Three.js, imported from a CDN, with no build step and no asset files. The file has to open in a browser and just run.\n\nSo far it holds worlds from 30 models across 12 labs, including Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, xAI, Meta and DeepSeek, and the site gets about 5K visits/month.\n\n### The Website\n\nworldbench.krishbakshi.com is where people use it:\n\n- Evaluations: every model's island runs live and interactive in the browser. Search or filter by lab, or open any world in its own window.\n- Compare: put up to six worlds side by side, in a link you can share.\n- Leaderboard: every scored model ranked, with each test broken out and the exact scores in a table.\n- About: what the benchmark tests, how scoring works, and how to cite it.\n\nThe scoring code is on GitHub, the results are a Hugging Face dataset, and the method is written up in the paper WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation (arXiv 2610.10622).\n\n---\n\nTitle: Campus Crew Program | Power Up Your Campus with HackerRank\nURL: https://www.hackerrank.com/campuscrew\nPublished: N/A\nAuthor: N/A\nHighlights:\nCampus Crew Program | Power Up Your Campus with HackerRank\n\n# Power Up Your Campus\n\nHost hackathons, guide peers, and build a stronger developer community as a HackerRank ambassador\n\n## About the program\n\nCampus Crew is HackerRank’s selective student ambassador program. They are passionate about technology, and should be deftly able to plan events and manage budgets.\n\n- Avid Learners: They are veritable experts that anyone can turn to for assistance.\n- Passionate Advocates: Actively promote `fastn` across communities, forums & events within their college / university.\n- Strong Organizers: Have the ability to conduct workshops, hackathons & learning sessions resulting in tangible outcomes.\n- Savvy Marketers: Have a way of handling promotions and marketing events across social channels to generate heightened participation.\n\n...\n\nFor all the time & effort you put in, `fastn` commits to help you gain an worthwhile advantage, when it comes to building your career and network. `fastn` supports Ambassadors in many ways. This group has access to special `fastn` projects & giveaways!\n- Shout-out & Endorsement: Your work and your profile is put on a pedestal! You will receive official `fastn` certificates and accreditation to bolster your achievements.\n- fastn Ambassador NFT: You will unlock a special fastn NFT, tailor-made for Ambassadors. This super-cool NFT will provide you access to a select fastn reward bundles & giveaways.\n- Career Opportunities: For Ambassadors who display outstanding levels of commitment & results, `fastn` will promote you to our Clients & Partner network as a fastn-certified potential hire. On successful selection, Ambassadors will be able to work full-time/part-time or as a consultant across active projects.\n- IRL Ambassador Upskilling: Ambassadors will attend periodic \"Ambassadors All-Hands\" & \"Train the trainer\" events at different locations around the country. This will allow them to forge a strong network as well build a cohesive array of managerial skills to augment your developer skills.\n- Event Support: All Ambassadors, get access to `fastn` Event Set-Up Kits that would allow them to set up and create fastn workshops on the fly. Consistent performers would get instant access to sponsorships, swag material & rewards to assist their event management capabilities.\n- Major Developer Events: Selective Ambassadors would be chosen to represent fastn across major developer events in the country. Tickets, stay and travel would be handled by the fastn team on their behalf. \n\n# How to become a `fastn` Ambassador?\n\nTo become an Ambassador, we ask you to demonstrate your power to structure, organize, manage & communicate. All participant details / repos are to be shared across the Discord channel provided earlier. Success of the event will be based on the work submitted by the participants. Apart from the `fastn` basics, you are to emphasize on the `fastn` Champions program and drive spirited participation.\n- `fastn` Campus Contest: All participants from hands-on workshop are further encouraged to take part in a contest. Winners from the contest have to fulfil a creative challenge, based on the things they learnt from the workshop. Two active Aliit Fellows share a candid look at what it takes to get accepted, what you'll actually build, and how contributing to the ecosystem opens real-world career opportunities. \n\nDevelopers weighing whether to apply to Aliit, Midnight's developer ambassador program, tend to hit the same wall. Plenty of curiosity, but the only information within reach is the program overview. So Midnight Korea went straight to two active Aliit members and asked what they actually do, what it took to get in, and what they got out of it.\n\n...\n\n## You may be more ready than you think\n\nBoth of them, unprompted, named the same misconception: that Aliit is only open to developers who are already at the top.\n\nAlex took it step by step. He completed the Midnight Academy courses, joined the NightForce ambassador program to get a feel for the community, and only then applied to Aliit. He spoke to no one before being accepted, and the whole process took about a month from application to acceptance.\n\nNorman applied after two Midnight hackathons and an email inviting him to Aliit cohort 0. He was upfront about his intentions: build DApps for mobile, and bring Midnight to communities in Mexico and Latin America. He wasn't sure he was ready, but he went for it anyway.\n\nThere was no secret threshold they had to meet. The requirement was simple: show that you are a real developer who wants to learn ZK and build something on Midnight Network. As Alex learned, the program welcomes any developer with the will to learn.\n\n\"They think it is only for developers that are already in the TOP.\" — Alex\n\n## What an Aliit Fellow actually does\n\nThere are two stages. You start as a Builder, and some go on to become Fellows.\n\nAs a Builder, you work through Zealy quests to reach 1,500 points and qualify for Fellow review. The quests cover a wide range, so you pick what fits you: education, documentation, bug fixes across the Midnight toolset, technical writing. Coding is a given. To qualify, you need to finish at least one meaningful coding task.\n\nOnce you're a Fellow, the fixed structure falls away. Alex, now a Fellow, works entirely self-directed and files a monthly report on his technical contributions. Norman estimates that about 99% of his work is self-directed. You decide what matters to the ecosystem and plan your own contributions. Writing code for Midnight remains mandatory. There is no minimum number of hours or lines, but moving up means showing growing impact month over month.\n\n...\n\nThere is no fixed weekly time commitment. Norman runs several projects at once and puts in more than 20 hours a week, but says around 5 is enough if you focus on a single project. Alex points to the one thing he wishes he'd known: you only really understand the time commitment once you're in.\n\n...\n\n## What to know before you apply\n\nBoth were clear about who should not apply.\n\nIf you're after an immediate financial reward, this program isn't for you. If you want to build quietly on your own, it probably isn't either. The ambassador role is not a side detail. Helping others learn, use, and succeed on Midnight Network is the core of what an Aliit Fellow does.\n\n\"If you are just a developer that wants to build on your own, probably the Aliit is not for you.\" — Alex\n\n...\n\n## How to start now\n\nIf you're interested in Aliit but still hesitating, both suggest a simple way to start without making a big commitment.\n\nMidnight Awesome DApps repo\n\nStart by going to dev-chat in the Midnight Discord and reading the problems other developers post. If you find yourself wanting to solve one of them, that's a good sign. Then browse the Awesome DApps repo. If you find yourself thinking, I want to build something like this, you probably already have your answer.\n\nIf you feel you're not ready, Alex points to the Midnight Academy courses.\n\nMidnight Academy\n\nNorman puts it differently: you're never really ready. Pick a problem you want to solve in the privacy space, write down what you'd need to solve it, and that list becomes your roadmap. Once you start working on the problem, the question of whether you're ready enough fades on its own.\n\nNorman applied with a personal goal no one assigned him: bringing Midnight to developers in Mexico and Latin America (LATAM), in their own language and context. Alex believes local communities are the key to worldwide adoption. Read their words side by side and the same message surfaces. The ecosystem is early enough that whoever builds the tools, content, and community for their region gets noticed right away.\n\nFor every developer interested in Midnight, that seat is open right now. It could be you.\n\n---\n\nTitle: Midnight blog | Midnight Foundation launches quests in advance of Fellowship program\nURL: https://midnight.network/blog/midnight-foundation-launches-quests-in-advance-of-ambassador-program\nPublished: 2025-09-25T15:55:30.000Z\nAuthor: Midnight\nHighlights:\n# Midnight Foundation launches quests in advance of Fellowship program\n\nUPDATE:\n\nDisclaimer: Since this blog was originally published, the Developer Ambassador program has become the Midnight Aliit Fellowship program.\n\nSeptember 25th, 2025\n\nThe Midnight Foundation has introduced community and builder quests, which are now available on Zealy, a platform used to host community engagement programs. 在学校成立HCSD社团或可将HCSD挂靠至计算机协会/技术社团等单位，并邀请一名本校在职老师作为HCSD指导老师（必备）\n\n③ 已签署华为开发者协议并加入华为开发者计划（必备）\n\n④ 熟悉掌握一项或多项华为云开放能力（必备）\n\n⑤ 作为高校技术社团的组织者或核心成员，具备带领和指导社团成员围绕华为技术开放能力进行学习、交流和创新实践的经验\n\n⑥ 利用华为技术开放能力在开发者社区/开源社区有一定的成果和技术影响力\n\n⑦ 多次主导组织或参与技术相关活动/大赛，并取得一定成绩\n\n⑧ 具备一定的组织能力，有协助开展校园开发者活动、推广大赛和雇主品牌的经历。\n\n...\n\n## 常见问题\n\nHCSD是一个什么样的组织？\n\nHCSD （华为云学生开发者计划）Huawei Cloud Student Developers是由校园大使为代表的校园开发者组织，致力于连接高校师生和云服务，通过互动交流、学习内容共享、实践项目建设，影响并帮助高校学生在云服务领域进行学习和创新。\n\n成为校园大使需要具备的条件？\n\n1.必须是在校学生，校园达人，有一定的影响力，计算机协会/技术社团负责人优先；\n\n2.计算机/信息技术相关专业；热爱前沿技术和开发，认可华为云开发者生态，勇于探索，敢于创新；\n\n3.执行力MAX，有想法，有创意，社交技能强，善于团队协作，乐于分享；\n\n4.具备团队管理运营能力，包括活动组织、扩大HCSD规模、提升HCSD成员数等；\n\n如何选拔华为云校园大使？\n\n华为云校园大使可以通过两种方式选拔：第一种是由华为合作院校推荐，第二种是由个人自主申请。两种方式提交上来的候选人都需要经过资格初审、专家复审/面试/综合终评最终选拔出华为云校园大使。\n\n审核结果何时以什么方式公布？\n\n个人自主申请审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，30个工作日内完成审核；华为合作院校推荐的审核结果从收到候选人认证资料后，15个工作日内完成审核。\n\n华为云校园大使有效期多长？\n\n华为云校园大使从获得认证的日期开始，一个自然年为一个认证周期，在此期间，享有华为云校园大使荣誉称号及相应权益；到期后，将根据期间的贡献和成就，重新评估华为云校园大使的资格。\n\n---\n\nTitle:
